clue.text: Criminal activity in which a prince engaged

definitions.text: Criminal activity in which a prince engaged

parts.words: Criminal activity in which a prince engaged
parts.note: extortion by threat, read a second way as the dark armour the Black Prince (Edward, son of Edward III) is said to have fought in

explanation.surface: A royal has been caught up in some crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward the Black Prince, a medieval English heir, was traditionally named for his black armour, so the dark mail he fought in splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Extorting money by threatening to reveal secrets is a crime.

clue.text: Ship-building, in Yorkshire?

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
a house is a building

explanation.surface: Shipyards in a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighouse is a town in West Yorkshire, which has no shipyards; its name splits into a ship and a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a Yorkshire town whose name is made of a vessel and a dwelling.

clue.text: A Glaswegian maybe ? Of course!

definitions.meaning: a person from Glasgow is one example of a Scotsman
a racecourse, the famous one in Berkshire

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a Scotsman such as a Glaswegian; as one it is the Berkshire racecourse of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Wood, perhaps, is the sort to get fish

parts.note: kind means sort, as in 'that kind of thing'
a ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Is the forest the kind of place to go fishing?
explanation.definitionFit: Small sticks used to start a fire are typically pieces of timber.

clue.text: Ruth — a sea nymph in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise is changed in appearance, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ruth is really a mermaid wearing a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disguise' rearranges RUTH A SEA. Arethusa was a nymph of Greek myth turned into a spring.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Arethusa was a Nereid transformed into a fountain.

clue.text: Youth in German capital billed as cargo

parts.note: a lad is a youth
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the capital letter of German is G

explanation.surface: A young man in Berlin was charged as freight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' is not Berlin or Bonn but the first letter of German.
explanation.definitionFit: Lading is freight loaded on a ship, as in a bill of lading.

clue.text: Like filling one container from another

indicators.note: one word filling another means it is placed inside that word

parts.note: a bin is a container
as means like, as in 'as good as new'

explanation.surface: Decanting the contents of one vessel into another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' puts AS inside BIN; the definition 'another' means another container, a basin.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a bowl, another kind of vessel besides the bin.

clue.text: Dance wear ?

definitions.meaning: a Spanish dance in triple time

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a lively Spanish dance and a short jacket worn open.

clue.text: Killer is a foreigner, about fifty

indicators.note: about here means round, so one word goes around another

parts.note: a stranger is someone from elsewhere, a foreigner
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: The murderer turns out to be an outsider of around fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like an age approximation but puts STRANGER round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A murderer who throttles victims is a killer.

clue.text: Sounds a dandy poet !

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: Beau Nash was the famous 18th-century dandy of Bath

explanation.surface: A fashionable fop who writes verse sounds good.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Nashe was an Elizabethan writer; his name is pronounced like Beau Nash's.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Nashe was an Elizabethan pamphleteer and versifier.

clue.text: Odour of sanctity — how it might anger one

definitions.meaning: the fragrant smoke burnt at church services
as a verb stressed on the second syllable, it means to make furious

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is perfumed smoke used in worship; the verb means to enrage, a different word spelt the same.

clue.text: Does without money or a girl

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go round others

parts.note: taken as written
L, for pound (librum), is money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone doing without cash, or a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, so DOES goes round L and OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolores is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Help to remove piano and rearrange accommodation

indicators.note: rearrange tells us to put the remaining letters in a new order
remove tells us to take a letter out of the word before it

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: Instructions for a removal man: take the piano away and move the furniture around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove' takes P from HELP to leave HEL; with TO, 'rearrange' turns HELTO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel provides lodging for travellers.

clue.text: Rustic crane shifted obstacle

parts.note: a hind is a farm labourer or country peasant

indicators.note: shifted means the letters are moved into a different order

explanation.surface: A country bird moved, causing a blockage.
explanation.walkthrough: HIND is an old word for a farmhand; 'shifted' makes RANCE from CRANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance is something that gets in the way, an impediment.

clue.text: One to carry on is a politician

indicators.note: a word that carries others holds them inside itself

parts.note: a unit is a single thing, one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps going counts as a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' puts ON and IS inside UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a party favouring union, such as Ulster's or Britain's Conservative and Unionist Party, is a politician.

clue.text: Where I chuck my weight about in London

definitions.text: Where I chuck my weight about in London

parts.note: taken as written
to sling is to throw, chuck
a ton is a weight

explanation.surface: A London district where someone throws their weight around.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a borough of north London; read the name as I, SLING (throw) and TON (a weight).
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a London district whose name is a person throwing a heavy weight.

clue.text: Stupid fellow brought up on land?

definitions.meaning: a lump of earth turned up by the plough, read as if describing a farm-raised person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dull oaf and a lump of soil thrown up from a field.

clue.text: Girl's service book in the boot

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, so a girl's is Di's
a missal is the book of the Mass

explanation.surface: A woman's prayer book is in the car's luggage space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boot' looks like a car's luggage compartment but means being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the boot is slang for being fired from a job.

clue.text: Report a killer in the end

parts.note: a bullet is a thing that kills
taken as written

explanation.surface: Telling of a murderer at the end of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end' links: a bullet in someone is the end of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short news statement or announcement.

clue.text: Knew old song of the climber ?

parts.note: wist is an archaic past tense of wit, to know
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Was a mountaineer familiar with an old tune?
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' is not a mountaineer but a climbing plant, the old spelling of wisteria.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistaria is a twining plant that climbs walls.

clue.text: Measures taken in the fifties, say

indicators.note: say tells us the letters are pronounced rather than written

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty, so fifties are Ls

explanation.surface: Some sizes recorded during the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of the letter L, spoken, sounds like the answer; 'the fifties' looks like the decade but means more than one Roman fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old unit of cloth length, about 45 inches.

clue.text: Butler's work needs a brush ? I'd change that

indicators.note: change tells us to reorder the letters of the words before

explanation.surface: Does the manservant's job require a broom? I'd alter that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' is Samuel Butler, the 17th-century satirist, not a servant; 'change' rearranges A BRUSH I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler wrote the mock-heroic poem of that title.

clue.text: Many cut as meat might be

parts.note: C, the Roman hundred, stands for many
hewed means cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Lots of slices, the way a butcher prepares meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat is worked over by the teeth in eating, ground up in the mouth.

clue.text: Tree is backward — no catch !'

indicators.note: backward means the letters of both words are read from the end

parts.note: nay means no
to nab is to catch

explanation.surface: A tree is slow-growing, without a doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns NAYNAB end to end.
explanation.definitionFit: The banyan is an Indian fig tree with aerial roots.

clue.text: Striker's aim — to keep fit?

parts.note: a boxer's training target, a suspended bag struck to stay in condition, read as if a footballer's goal

explanation.surface: A footballer aims to stay in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer hits this inflated training bag to keep in condition.

clue.text: Some novel attendants ?

definitions.meaning: boys who serve a knight or noble

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both sheets of a book and young servants at court.

clue.text: Goodbye, said he, yet looked to its return

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: return means the letters of the word before are read backwards

explanation.surface: A man bids farewell yet still looks forward to coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns ITS to STI after TO. Paolo Tosti composed the famous Victorian song 'Goodbye!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian composer Paolo Tosti wrote the ballad 'Goodbye!', so he is the one who said it.

clue.text: Notes on fish?

definitions.meaning: a run of musical notes in order
the plates covering a fish's skin

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an ordered series of notes and one of the plates on a fish's body.

clue.text: Escape ? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: a flight from the scene, as of robbers
the exclamation of disbelief, as in 'you're kidding'

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a flight from capture; spoken as two words it is a cry of disbelief.

clue.text: Wound on the head ?

parts.note: wound read as the past of wind (wrapped), not as an injury

explanation.surface: An injury to the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lengths of cloth wrapped round the head as headwear.

clue.text: Meeting in the embassy, no doubt

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A conference at the embassy, surely.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church officials.

clue.text: Type of apron-line is 'unique

indicators.note: a type of something is a version of it, so these letters are recast into another form

explanation.surface: A kind of apron is one of a kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type of' rearranges APRON and LINE. The answer is also a small printing type size, so 'Type' doubles the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without equal, peerless, is one of a kind.
